$comment: Deterministic keyword/regex lexicons for annual-report text (PDF route only). 'flags' become Opportunity-leg rules; every match is shown with the quoted sentence and its page. A sentence containing a negator shortly before the match (e.g. 'has not defaulted') is skipped. 'claims' are upbeat management statements shown against a contradicting figure. Patterns are case-insensitive.

flags.title: Auditor's opinion is modified
flags.pattern: \b(basis for qualified opinion|qualified opinion|adverse opinion|disclaimer of opinion)\b
flags.plain: The auditor did not give a clean opinion. This is the single strongest text signal in an annual report.
flags.innocent: A narrow qualification on one disputed item that management has explained and since resolved.
flags.nextStep: Read the 'Basis for qualified opinion' paragraph in full and size the amount against profit.

flags.title: Going-concern doubt
flags.pattern: \b(material uncertainty related to going concern|significant doubt (on|about|upon) the (company|group|holding company)('s|s)? ability to continue as (a )?going concern)\b
flags.plain: The report raises doubt about the company's ability to keep operating.
flags.innocent: A start-up or turnaround with committed funding from its parent.
flags.nextStep: Check the funding plan management cites and whether lenders have agreed to it.

flags.title: Emphasis of matter
flags.plain: The auditor drew readers' attention to a specific note without modifying the opinion.
flags.innocent: Often a routine pointer to a merger, a restatement of comparatives or a pending litigation.
flags.nextStep: Read the note the auditor points to.

flags.title: Auditor resigned or changed mid-term
flags.plain: The statutory auditor left before the end of the term.
flags.innocent: Mandatory rotation after the maximum tenure, or a firm merger.
flags.nextStep: Find the resignation letter filed with the stock exchange and the reason given.

flags.title: Default on loans or statutory dues
flags.pattern: \b(default(ed|s)? in (the )?(repayment|payment) of (loans?|borrowings?|interest|dues)|undisputed statutory dues[^.;]{0,80}outstanding for (a period of )?more than six months)\b
flags.plain: The report mentions a default on borrowings or long-overdue statutory dues.
flags.innocent: A short technical delay that was cured before the report date.
flags.nextStep: Check the amount, the lender and whether the default was continuing at year-end.

flags.title: Loans or guarantees to related parties
flags.pattern: \b(loans?( and advances)?( given| granted| provided)? to (related parties|promoters?|directors?|(companies|firms|entities|parties) in which (the )?directors? (are|is) interested)|corporate guarantees? (given|issued|provided) (on behalf of|for|to) (related parties|group companies|subsidiaries|promoter))\b
flags.plain: Money or guarantees have gone to parties connected with the promoters or directors.
flags.innocent: Funding of a wholly owned subsidiary's project on arm's-length terms.
flags.nextStep: Size the balance against net worth using the related-party note and check repayments.

flags.title: Promoter share pledge mentioned
flags.pattern: \b(pledge of (the )?promoters?'? ?(group )?(equity )?shares|shares (held by|of) (the )?promoters?( and promoter group)? (have been|has been|are|were) pledged|promoters? (and promoter group )?(have|has) pledged|promoters?'? ?(group )?(share)?holding[^.;]{0,60}pledged)\b
flags.plain: The report mentions promoter shares pledged with lenders. (A subsidiary's own shares pledged as loan security is routine project finance and is not matched.)
flags.innocent: Pledges backing loans taken for the company's own expansion.
flags.nextStep: Enter the pledge percentage from the shareholding pattern on the confirm screen.

flags.title: Delayed filing or meeting
flags.plain: The report mentions a delayed filing, results or annual meeting.
flags.innocent: A regulator-wide extension (as in FY2020-FY2021) or a system outage.
flags.nextStep: Check stock-exchange announcements for the stated reason for the delay.

flags.title: Key audit matter on revenue or receivables
flags.plain: The auditor listed revenue, receivables or related parties as a key audit matter. Most reports do, so this is shown for information and carries no weight.
flags.innocent: Revenue is a presumed risk in almost every audit.
flags.nextStep: Read how the auditor says the matter was addressed.
